rationale: The literature confirms a broad phenotypic spectrum associated with SPTAN1 variants—spanning severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy with structural brain defects at one end to juvenile/adult-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN11 / HMND11) at the other. However, the hypothesis claims that dHMN11 is caused specifically by heterozygous missense or mild structural variants in non-critical domains. This is directly contradicted by reports demonstrating that heterozygous nonsense (premature truncation / loss-of-function) mutations in SPTAN1 cause dHMN (e.g., Dong et al., 2021; Beijer et al. as cited by Dohrn & Saporta, 2020). Therefore, while the broad genotype-phenotype gradient across SPTAN1 allelic disorders is supported, the variant-type restriction asserted in the hypothesis fails.

new_directions.question_text: Does SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency from nonsense-mediated mRNA decay specifically cause dHMN11, whereas dominant-negative interference with spectrin tetramerization causes severe epileptic encephalopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving whether nonsense variants leading to haploinsufficiency cause dHMN versus in-frame structural mutations driving dominant-negative protein aggregation will refine the true genotype-phenotype rule.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence of facial and neck flexor weakness in SPTAN1-associated dHMN11 across multi-center cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Identifying highly discriminative clinical features (such as neck flexor and facial weakness) helps clinicians distinguish dHMN11 from other axonal dHMN subtypes.
